old: The solver decides the puzzle edge by edge, either by deduction logic (see below), or by going edge by edge. For every edge between two tiles that has no wall already, it runs a very short search under each assumption: “a wall goes here” and “these two tiles are in the same piece”. If one assumption runs out of possibilities completely, the other one is certain. The idea being that a puzzle solvable by deduction would have a spot where you can easily find a way forward, and the solver tries to find it.
new: The solver decides the puzzle by finding the correct state for every edge (link or wall). Either by deduction logic, by going neighbors to neighbors, or by testing links between far away symbols. The global idea being that a puzzle solvable by deduction would have a breakthrough spot. The solver is designed to find it by attacking the puzzle with those approaches.

old: If the edge by edge isn’t enough the solver skips to a final solve and does an exhaustive search on the half done puzzle, hopefully finding an impossibility or a solution. The time percentage for the final solve is an estimate, not a truth. If the solver has trouble finding a solution after a minute, the puzzle probably requires a global thinking that the solver can’t find. If that is the case, please send your puzzle to nittneuk on discord so I can try to implement a reasoning for it.
new: If it can't find a breakthrough in the current puzzle state, the solver skips to a final solve and does an exhaustive search on the half done puzzle, hopefully finding an impossibility or a solution. If the solver has trouble finding a solution after a minute of exhaustive search, the puzzle probably requires a global thinking that the solver can’t find. If that is the case, please send your puzzle to me! (nittneuk on discord) so I can try to implement a reasoning for puzzle of it's kind.
